focal_entities.audience: the user approving the README at the design sign-off, and whoever makes the architecture and builds the tool to it

goal_orientation.purpose: deciding from the README whether it tells what the tool gives them and how to install and use it, approving it, and building the tool and its architecture to what it promises

goal_orientation.serves: AC11: A README says how to install the tool and how to use it.

constraints.decision: Language: The tool is written in Python, with its standard library alone; on macOS the user installs Python 3 first, such as with Xcode's command line tools or Homebrew.

How it is installed: The user installs the tool from GitHub with pipx in one line, pipx install "git+https://github.com/lovaizu/playground#subdirectory=organize-downloads", which puts the command on PATH and updates and removes it in one line too; pipx is installed first, such as with brew install pipx on macOS or apt install pipx on Linux, and uv tool install works the same way for those who use uv.
Command name: The command is named organize-downloads.

How moving and undo are typed: The explicit word to act is --apply, for organizing and undo alike: organize-downloads only lists, organize-downloads --apply moves, organize-downloads undo only lists what it would put back, organize-downloads undo --apply puts it back; a folder to organize instead of Downloads is given last on each.
License: The tool is released under the MIT license, kept in organize-downloads/LICENSE; the repository has no license of its own.

Where Documentation points: The README's Documentation points to organize-downloads --help for fuller use, such as same-named files, files left in place and which extensions go to which folder, and to the repository's commit history for what changed; what --help shows is still to be settled when the tool is built.
Copyright holder: The MIT license names lovaizu as the copyright holder: Copyright (c) 2026 lovaizu.
